# agents v0.8.1 — what `init` writes stops pointing at deleted files

A patch release. No command changed shape and no exit code moved. What changed is
the text the binary carries into the repositories it initializes.

## What changed

**The bundled skill no longer cites a deleted design.** `init` installs
`recording-what-you-learn`, and its closing section told the reader to consult
`docs/design/2026-08-19-knowledge-is-documentation.md` in the dotfiles
repository. That document was deleted on 2026-10-12, along with the system it
described. Every repository initialized from v0.8.0 therefore got a pointer to a
file that does not exist — the defect class this project removes, shipped inside
the artifact that distributes it. The section now says the evidence was in a
design since deleted, and that its last revision is in git history.

**The plans template carries the status rule.** `init` writes
`docs/plans/README.md` from an embedded template, and the template did not have
the rule the store itself follows: **every plan opens with a `Status:` line.**
Without one, a plan whose work finished years ago and a plan someone is about to
execute read the same, and the plans store is where a reader goes for what to do
next. New repositories get the rule now.

## Upgrading

```
brew upgrade agents
```

Nothing to convert. The chain record, the hooks path and `doctor`'s checks are
unchanged from v0.8.0, and this release changes no command's arguments, output
shape or exit codes.

An existing repository keeps the files it already has. `init` writes a store's
README and a skill only when the path is absent, so this release rewrites nothing
you have customized. To adopt either text in an existing repository, copy it from
`agents/internal/scaffold/assets/` in the dotfiles repository.

## Checks

`agents` 8 packages and `bootstrap.d` 6 packages, whole runs; the documents
guards; and the CI gate on Debian and Arch (stage zero included), macOS, and the
hygiene legs.
